about: Toolbox K2 (Rates and efficiencies): the one constant this page adds. Every other input is read from the data files of the lessons that use it (01-power-energy.json, 07-cost.json, 13-capstone.json, town.json, cf_targets.json), so the numbers stay the same as there.

btuPerKWh.unit: Btu per kWh (equivalently 3.412 MMBtu per MWh)
btuPerKWh.what: The energy content of one kilowatt-hour of electricity, in British thermal units. Efficiency of a power plant = 3,412 Btu divided by its heat rate in Btu per kWh.
btuPerKWh.source: EIA, Frequently Asked Questions: What is the efficiency of different types of power plants?

batteryNote: The 85% round trip is lesson 13's battery (NREL's 2025 battery cost study, in 13-capstone.json). Lesson 9's illustrative battery uses 80%, near the 82% EIA measured for U.S. utility-scale batteries in 2019.
co2Note: CO2 per MWh is heat rate x EIA's 52.91 kg CO2 per MMBtu of natural gas, as lessons 12 and 13 compute it: operating emissions at the plant only. Lesson 0's Prairie Town fleet uses a rounded illustrative 0.37 t per MWh for its combined-cycle plant.
